How to read the visual hints

Green tiles indicate letters confirmed in their correct slots. These anchors matter most when starting—you can build outward from any solid green position. Yellow tiles show letters that exist somewhere in the word but haven't found home yet. Gray tiles are simply in the way.

Drag letters to swap them. The system highlights valid drops. Focus on completing one direction first—usually whichever has more greens showing—and let those placements constrain the perpendicular words.

Common wrong approaches

Treating each row independently causes conflicts. Because shared letters must work for both directions, solving horizontally first and vertically second creates contradictions you'll have to undo. Instead, identify intersection points early and lock those first.

Another frequent mistake: guessing based on vowel density alone. Consonants carry the structural weight in most Waffle words. A word like CRANE needs R and N almost as much as the vowels—don't deprioritize them.

Players also stumble by ignoring word frequency. Common entries appear far more often than obscure ones. If you've got _R__E and _A__N, CRANE fits better than PRANK or GRIND in most puzzles.

Should I start from corners or edges?

Neither is universally better, but corners give you two directional constraints immediately. An anchored corner letter limits both its row and column simultaneously. Edges offer similar advantages if the corner isn't showing greens yet.

Standard daily mode allows 15 swaps. That's enough for most solvers who approach methodically, but wasteful play drains it fast. Track your swaps consciously—if you're past 10 with unsolved rows, reconsider your strategy.

The daily resets at midnight in your local timezone. Failed attempts don't carry over, but neither do partial solutions. Check the archive linked above to review today's exact layout when the new puzzle drops.
